title: Habitat use and morphological evolution in Sceloporus: a single- and multi-trait comparative analysis
content:
Abstract
Analyses of body shape and its relationship to habitat use are essential to understanding the process of biological adaptation. Habitat use is one of the main factors influencing body shape variation in lizards, resulting in a wide range of morphological responses to different selection pressures associated with locomotion across diverse substrates. In this study, we examined the evolutionary dynamics of eight morphological traits (derived from 11 measured traits after averaging left–right pairs) across 79 species of the genus Sceloporus. Using a suite of phylogenetic comparative methods, we tested whether habitat use drives morphological differentiation independently of phylogenetic relatedness. Our results indicate that although Sceloporus shows dynamic morphological evolution associated with habitat use, this pattern is not clear when multiple traits are analysed simultaneously. However, trait-specific analyses revealed associations between habitat type and traits such as head width and snout–vent length. These findings suggest that morphological similarity among species occupying similar environments might result from adaptive responses to habitat use, regardless of phylogenetic history. We discuss potential selective pressures and evolutionary mechanisms underlying these patterns of morphological evolution in Sceloporus.
